extracted.intended_audience: organizations and practitioners that publish fact-checks (fact-checkers, newsrooms, media organizations)
extracted.subtask_description: A set of organizational commitments and standards for groups that regularly publish nonpartisan fact-checks of public claims, describing required practices on nonpartisanship, source transparency, funding transparency, methodology, and corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonpartisanship and Fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: Signatory organizations fact-check claims using the same standard for every fact check. They do not concentrate their fact-checking on any one side. They follow the same process for every fact check and let the evidence dictate the conclusions. Signatories do not advocate or take policy positions on the issues they fact-check.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies the same standards and processes across subjects and actors; avoid selective targeting; conclusions must be evidence-driven; avoid advocacy or taking policy positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of Sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Signatories want their readers to be able to verify findings themselves. Signatories provide all sources in enough detail that readers can replicate their work, except in cases where a source’s personal security could be compromised. In such cases, signatories provide as much detail as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish sources and sufficient citation/detail to enable reader verification and replication; if security risks exist for a source, redact identifying details but still disclose as much as feasible and explain limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of Funding & Organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Signatory organizations are transparent about their funding sources. If they accept funding from other organizations, they ensure that funders have no influence over the conclusions the fact-checkers reach in their reports. Signatory organizations detail the professional background of all key figures in the organization and explain the organizational structure and legal status. Signatories clearly indicate a way for readers to communicate with them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose funding sources and organizational/legal structure; document key personnel backgrounds; guard editorial independence from funders and explain how influence is prevented; provide clear contact channels for readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of Methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Signatories explain the methodology they use to select, research, write, edit, publish and correct their fact checks. They encourage readers to send claims to fact-check and are transparent on why and how they fact-check.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish clear methodological descriptions covering selection criteria, research methods, writing and editing processes, publication workflow, and correction procedures; invite reader submissions and explain selection rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open & Honest Corrections Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Signatories publish their corrections policy and follow it scrupulously. They correct clearly and transparently in line with the corrections policy, seeking so far as possible to ensure that readers see the corrected version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a published corrections policy and implement corrections openly and promptly; ensure corrected versions are visible to readers and linked to original content where appropriate.
